Welcome to your first night shift, Operator.

YOUR TASKS appear in the Work Queue window (top right) and on the taskbar when you click Begin. Do them in order. Each task has a hint under it.

- Double-click an icon or a file to open it.
- Workstation opens File Manager: your folders and files.
- Drag a window by its title bar to move it.
- Drag a file onto a folder to move it there.
- Drag a file onto the Disposal bin to shred it.
- If another pointer grabs a file you are dragging, hold the button and drag along the arrow until the bar is yours, then let go on the folder or bin.
- If mail says to let the other pointer finish, let it. But if a task tells you to shred a file, hold on and fight for it.
- Right-click anything to see what you can do.
- Esc or the || button on the taskbar: pause and Options.
- NEXUS Help (on the desktop) explains everything else.

Some programs need clearance you do not have. Stick to your tasks.

NEXUS OS 4.1 -- QUICK HELP

YOUR SHIFT: your tasks are in the Work Queue (top right, or the Task button on the taskbar). Do them in order; the hint under each task says how. A task marked (remote session) was added by another session, not by Night Operations: you decide whether to do it.

OPEN: Double-click an icon or file to open it.
MOVE A WINDOW: Drag it by its title bar.
MOVE FILES: Double-click Workstation to open File Manager, click a folder on the left, then drag a file onto another folder.
SHRED: Drag a file onto the Disposal bin, then click Yes.
WORK ORDERS: Look the owner up in Personnel, then click Approve or Reject.
TUG-OF-WAR: if another pointer grabs a file you are dragging, keep the mouse button held and drag firmly the way the arrow on the file points. The bar above it shows who is winning: once your side passes the line, the file is yours, and letting go drops it on the folder or bin under the pointer. Let go before that and the other pointer keeps it. The first fight of a night starts with a moment to read. Mail may tell you to let the other pointer finish: let it move things on its own, but when a task tells you to shred a file, fight for it.
JOTTER: if a remote session types to you in Jotter, type a reply and press Enter. While it is typing, your reply waits. Your typing goes to the Jotter that is waiting for you, even when another window is in front.
CAMERAS: Camera Viewer shows the security cameras. Click a camera on the left to switch. Another session can close the viewer: double-click Camera Viewer to open it again.
LOCKED FOLDERS: some folders ask for a code. Type the code and press Enter.
SAVING: some files can be changed in Jotter. Typing starts a new line at the end; use File > Save (or Ctrl+S) to keep it.
NEXUS MENU: the Nexus button (bottom left) lists every program, Help and Shut Down. At the end of a shift it also holds Log Off.
OPTIONS: Right-click an item to see what you can do with it. Esc or the || button on the taskbar pauses the shift.

NEXUS OS records all activity for quality purposes.

SECOND CURSOR is a work of fiction. The game does not read your files, move your real mouse, or use your camera or microphone. Every name, company and event in it is invented. Everything that happens here happens inside the game.

Photosensitivity warning: this game contains flickering, screen glitches and sudden loud sounds. You can reduce flashing at any time in Options (Esc, or the || button on the taskbar).

SECOND CURSOR

A game about sharing a desk with someone who never logged off.

Design, writing, code, pixel art and sound were made for this game. Every sound is generated while you play.

Made with Unity.

Letheworth Data Reclamation, NEXUS OS, Orrery Computing and everyone who works there are invented. Any resemblance to a real night shift is a coincidence.

Thanks to every night operator who tested an early build.
